editorial:
Imagine going back to the place where you grew up, only to find that everything you loved has changed. That is exactly what happens to Rina and her son, Facundo. They head back to the Tigre river Delta, a beautiful area full of water and greenery, hoping to reclaim their old home. You will feel the tension right away because the vibe is heavy and uneasy. It is not just about family drama; there is a sense of danger in the air as the river rises and the natural world starts to feel unpredictable and scary.

What really makes this work is the acting and the way the camera captures the river. The pacing is a bit slow, which might be a turn-off if you want constant action, but it builds a great mood. The struggle between nature and the machines coming in to destroy the land feels very real. If you enjoy slow-burn stories about family and loss, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a heavy note as the water continues to rise and the forest feels more like a trap than a home. Rina and Facundo realize they cannot truly go back to the way things were. After the tension with the missing girl and the encroaching machinery, they face the hard truth that their past is gone. They are left to deal with the loss of their home while the environment around them changes forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quiet dramas about family secrets and nature.
